sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.,Sujata Choudhary Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Donadi Ramesh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Ms. Sujata Choudhary, learned counsel for respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Petitioners have applied for issuance of passport as their daughter is getting married in U.S.A. on 21st April, 2025.
In response to such application, the passport authorities have issued a notice seeking clarification from the petitioners in respect of two criminal cases instituted against them.

sentences.text:

498A, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3, 4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Ghaziabad, the petitioners have already been acquitted, whereas in respect of proceedings of other case instituted pursuant to the direction of the Magistrate under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C., the further proceedings of Criminal Case No. 3882 of 2021 (State Vs. Amit Tyagi and others) has been stayed until further order of the Court.

entities.text: State Vs. Amit Tyagi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that in view of the orders passed by the competent Court, there is no basis for the passport authorities to withhold the issuance of passport to the petitioners.
Learned counsel for the respondents states that if such facts are placed before the concerned respondents, they shall do the needful.
In that view of the matter, we permit the petitioner to approach second respondent along with a copy of this order annexing all materials in support of their claim, as is noticed above.

The second respondent will examine such matters and would ensure that appropriate order as is required is passed in respect of issuance of passport to the petitioners, within a period of one week from the date of representation of this order.
Accordingly, the present writ petition is disposed of.
